Families: groups and clusters

Source: vignettes/clusters.Rmd
clusters.Rmd

Layers decide which organizations a record can be matched to, and name and address classes decide which strings each one carries - see vignette("layers"), vignette("sources") and vignette("corroborators"). Families answer a third question: when no single EIN can be chosen, which set of EINs can.

A chapter of a federation, a hospital and its system, a school and its PTO: the evidence is often split, the name matching one organization and the address another, so no candidate scores as a match while the family plainly does. matchdb groups EINs so that the matcher can stop one level up.

Two derived tables hold that grouping, and they are not the same thing.

built by id what it means
entity_group md_build_groups() group_id one federated family, from the group-exemption edges in ein_relation
cluster, cluster_member, cluster_footprint md_build_clusters() cluster_id six types of family, including the groups above, each EIN in as many as apply

Neither stores anything query-dependent. Both are facts about the database; the matcher does the rest.

The counts below are from the build of 2026-11-01 (matchdb@d632f21, normalizer v1-592912060053c4c3).

group_id: the federated families

md_build_groups() takes the connected components of the group_member edges in ein_relation. Two EINs are in the same family exactly when they share a group_id, so “are these two candidates the same family?” becomes one join.

group_member edges: 453,568, of which 447,311 are used and 6,257 set aside
entity_group: 450,964 EINs in 3,700 groups (5 passes)
  group size: median 16, largest 17,902

Each row carries ein, group_id, group_size, role (parent, member or both), n_parents, and group_central_ein - the parent with the most members. EINs in no group get no row, so a LEFT JOIN from entity gives them NULL.

group_id is "GRP-" plus the digits of the smallest EIN in the component, e.g. GRP-01-0347504. It depends only on membership, so rebuilding gives the same ids and adding an unrelated group moves no existing one - unlike a row number. It carries no other meaning: the smallest EIN is usually a member, not the parent. Use group_central_ein for that.

Why components, not the group exemption number. One logical group already spans several GENs (Lions 4, AAU 7, 4-H 12), and Rev. Proc. 2026-8 makes central organizations drop all but one ruling by 2027-01-22. A central EIN holding several GENs links them all, and a member listed under two parents joins their groups - both of which a GEN key would miss.

One bad edge joins two families, so evidence is ranked. A filer writes another group’s GEN on line H(c), by typo or from an old ruling, and in the first full build a high-school orchestra became a member of both a youth soccer league and Parent Booster USA: one component of 25,739 EINs joining the US Catholic Conference, the Mayo Clinic, a sorority and a motorcycle club. Each member’s edges are now filtered before the components are taken, keeping only its best-ranked evidence: the IRS’s own coding first, then the parent’s roster on its group return, then an older GEN assignment, then the member’s own line H(c). The first two are kept whole - a member the IRS or its parent places in two groups is a real link. From the self-reported ranks a member keeps one parent. The 6,257 set-aside edges stay in ein_relation; only the components ignore them.

cluster_id: six types of family

md_build_clusters() writes one row per cluster, one per cluster and EIN, and one per cluster, layer and state. An EIN can belong to many clusters of different types.

type prefix clusters memberships median largest built from
group_exemption GRP- 3,700 450,962 16 17,902 entity_group, above
related_system SYS- 95,283 1,077,889 2 1,023 Schedule R, one star per discloser
care_of_network ICO- 2,648 8,818 2 265 in-care-of values naming one other organization
shared_website WEB- 30,722 108,075 2 1,557 website or email-domain keys held by 2+ EINs
brand BRD- 531 351,921 78 25,276 a concentrated name word
co_tenant CTN- 665,578 1,468,118 2 3 a shared street address

Together: 798,462 clusters over 1,655,813 EINs.

cluster carries cluster_id, cluster_type, central_ein (NULL where the type has none), size, label and brand_tokens - the name words held by at least half the members of a cluster of three or more, most shared first, which is what a cluster-level name comparison looks for: ROTARY, not CLUB. cluster_member carries role (central, parent, intermediate, member) and evidence. cluster_footprint counts members per cluster, layer and state; layers partition EINs, so the footprint of any layer selection is the exact sum of its rows, the same rule as ein_key_layer.

Clustering by address

co_tenant is the type built from addresses, and it is much the largest.

The key is the one npnormalize produces: street_key and zip5, stored in ein_key under kind place (see md_place_key()), so a lookup from npmatch never misses on spelling. A cluster forms where 2 to max_cotenants EINs (3 by default) report the same place as their own current address. A grantmaker writing a grantee’s address is not occupancy.

Shared places of four or more are mostly registered agents, processing centres and national headquarters, which say nothing about affiliation. Stopping at three is what keeps this a family rather than a mailing list: 852K pairs sit at places shared by 2-3 EINs, and only 5.7% of those pairs are already in ein_relation, so this is the largest new source of family links - and the least verified of the six.

The place class gates it. Where md_build_places() has run, a co-tenant family forms only at a place whose place_class is cluster and which is not flagged care_of, cmra or agent_churn. An accountant’s c/o address, a mailbox store or an agent’s address with a churning client list holds unrelated organizations however few of them there are.

place_class is npnormalize’s own address classification, the four labels np_addr_freq() returns, rebuilt over the database by the same rule and thresholds:

place: 278,930 shared places (cluster 268,801, building 4,873,
       shared 2,824, federated 2,432); place_unit: 35,439 shared suites
  • federated - crowded, and one name dominates: a national office its chapters file from.
  • building - crowded, with two or more recorded suites and enough suite coverage to believe them.
  • shared - crowded, names spread: a fiscal sponsor or an agent.
  • cluster - a handful of EINs, usually an organization with its foundation. This is the only class that becomes a family.

The place table adds what the run-time statistic cannot see: private-mailbox suites, in-care-of agents, bank and trust shares, group rulings among the occupants, and churn over every EIN that has ever had the address. Those are the flags above.

Which package does what

The grouping is split across the stack on purpose, and the id is only ever assigned in one place.

package its part assigns an id?
npnormalize the keys the grouping groups on (street_key, street_unit_id, zip5, name_key) and np_addr_freq(), a per-address statistic no
matchdb builds and stores group_id and cluster_id yes
npmatch reads them at match time: np_pair_links(), np_cluster_rollup() no
pfmatch its own query-side identity collapse, pf_dedup() to recipient_uid yes, but of grant rows, not of EINs

The last row is a different layer, easily confused with this one. pfmatch groups its own records - repeated grant rows that are one recipient - on (name_key, street_key, zip5), so that a match found for any member propagates to all of them. matchdb groups reference EINs into families. A pfmatch run uses both.

Using them

A compiled reference carries the families of the organizations in it:

b <- md_reference("active-observed", fetch = "missing")
b$clusters

npmatch reads that alongside the scored candidates. np_pair_links() reports whether a query’s top two candidates are one family - a tie between relatives is a family to settle, a tie between strangers is a real ambiguity - and np_cluster_rollup() handles split evidence. On 1,984 Schedule I records with a known EIN, the roll-up placed 60 of 739 non-YES records in a family, and the true EIN was in that family 90% of the time. vignette("matchdb") section 6 works through both.

To look at one organization’s families, md_cluster():

md_cluster("39-1925617", types = c("related_system", "shared_website"))
#> <md_cluster> EIN-39-1925617: 4 clusters (related_system 3, shared_website 1)
#>
#>   SYS-87-4664285  related_system, 2 members  BOYS & GIRLS CLUB OF DANE COUNTY FOUNDATION INC
#>       EIN-87-4664285  BOYS & GIRLS CLUB OF DANE COUNTY FOUNDAT WI
#>     * EIN-39-1925617  BOYS AND GIRLS CLUB OF DANE COUNTY INC WI
#>   ...

size always reports the full count, while max_members limits what is listed - a brand cluster can hold 25,000.

A narrow layer choice can split a family: a chapter may be bmf_inactive while its parent is bmf_active. md_compile() reports that in its absence report, per cluster type.

r <- md_compile(md_spec(layers = "bmf_active"))
r$report$absence

What each type had to be guarded against

  • related_system is a star, never a component. Chained together, Schedule R edges make one component of 117,869 EINs across the health and university sectors. Each discloser instead gets its own cluster of the entities it lists, and overlapping stars are kept as they are.
  • Most in-care-of values are not organizations. Of 1.6M values, 1.05M are people, 103K roles or titled people, 32K agents and 16K the organization’s own name. A value is used only when it is none of these, names exactly one EIN’s legal or dba name in two or more words, and is in the same state. The state rule is what separates a person from the eponymous foundation (CALVIN JONES / CALVIN JONES FOUNDATION). This type needs the peopleparser census name table.
  • brand took three passes. Letting every concentrated word be a brand gave STATES 42,951 EINs and CLUBS 40,685. One brand per dominant name, anchored on its most concentrated word, gave LIONS rather than CLUBS - but the anchor still took every use of the word, so COLUMBUS gathered Columbus, Ohio. An anchor with other uses now also needs a second word of the brand’s name, trailing S ignored: SPRINGFIELD LIONS CLUB is in, DETROIT LIONS and COLUMBUS SYMPHONY are not. This type is what reaches the 63% of Toastmasters clubs that are in no group exemption.
  • co_tenant stops at three, and reads the place class - above.

Placeholder EINs (0, 123456789) and EINs absent from entity are dropped from every type: a cluster holding a placeholder would be a false family. A star whose only listed entities fell outside entity is one EIN, not a cluster, and clusters of one are not written.

What this does not do

  • No levels. Clusters do not nest into chapter, state body and national.
  • No merging. Overlapping clusters are left overlapping; the consumer sees every membership and decides.
  • No scoring. What a family is worth is npmatch’s judgement, and np_cluster_rollup() annotates rather than changing the EIN-level tier. Whether a CLUSTER match counts as a resolution is the analysis’s choice.
  • Not fully validated. The brand and co-tenant types in particular should be checked against held-out federated cases before a matcher leans on them.

Rebuilding

Both builders drop and rebuild, and the order matters: md_build_groups() before md_build_clusters(), since group_exemption reads entity_group, and md_build_places() before it too, so that co_tenant can read the place class. md_build_groups() reads only ein_relation and keys on EINs rather than on reassigned row ids, so a re-ingest leaves it out of date rather than broken. Rebuild after any ingest that writes group_member edges.

con <- md_db()
md_build_groups(con)
md_build_places(con)
md_build_clusters(con)
md_db_close(con)
